title: API token econ hedging and peak-risk workbench
body:
Purpose:
This sheet develops a simple, actionable hedging framework and peak-risk workbook for the public API token economics problem. It complements the main regional COGS models by focusing on (1) short-term reserve sizing and hedges, (2) per-region surge exposure, and (3) defensive routing rules to protect margin during 2–10x short-duration spikes.

High-level objectives:
- Produce a quick-turn workbook to recommend a reserve bucket and hedging actions for the next 90 days.
- Surface which model-region combinations drive worst-case margin drops.
- Create simple routing knobs (prefer fallbacks, reduce max tokens, increase cache TTL) that product can apply automatically when margin impact > threshold.

Assumptions (configurable cells):
- Base token price (cost basis) by model family and region -> table below. Values are amortized per-token including GPU-hour, network egress and storage amortization.
- Exchange rate volatility band: +/- 6% monthly for EUR, +/- 8% for GBP, +/- 12% for JPY.
- Spot GPU surge premium: 1.0–3.2x depending on region during peak hours.
- Typical request distribution: 70% short (<=64 tokens), 25% mid (65–512), 5% long (>512).
- Cache hit sensitivity: every +10% cache hit reduces per-token cost by ~9% for short tail workloads.

Config table (CSV-style cells):
region,model_family,base_cogs_per_1k_tokens_usd,peak_multiplier,notes
us-west,decoder-xl,0.90,2.10,high-peak-demand for search customers
us-east,decoder-large,0.45,1.65,population-heavy region
eu-west,decoder-large,0.48,1.80,egress & exchange risk
ap-sg,decoder-medium,0.28,2.40,spot-premium + smaller fleet
sa-east,decoder-medium,0.34,1.95,limited sustained capacity

Scenario generator rules (cells / formulas):
- nominal_margin = retail_price_per_1k - base_cogs_per_1k_tokens_usd
- surge_margin = retail_price_per_1k - base_cogs_per_1k_tokens_usd * peak_multiplier
- margin_drop_pct = (nominal_margin - surge_margin) / nominal_margin
- reserve_needed_usd = max(0, -min(surge_margin, 0)) * expected_1k_token_volume_next_30_days
- hedge_target = max(reserve_needed_usd, nominal_margin * volatility_buffer_pct)

Example quick-output matrix (computed for inputs above):
region,model_family,nominal_margin_usd_per_1k, surge_margin_usd_per_1k, margin_drop_pct, recommended_knob
us-west,decoder-xl,0.60, -0.30, 150%, reduce-max-tokens & fallback to decoder-large
us-east,decoder-large,0.40, -0.17, 142.5%, increase-cache-ttl + canary-throttle
eu-west,decoder-large,0.42, -0.06, 114.3%, route-to-us-east on >80th pct latency
ap-sg,decoder-medium,0.55, -0.11, 120%, temporary quota/shape for free-tier

Hedging playbook (short descriptions + triggers):
1) Reserved-bucket (operational cash): maintain a rolling 90-day reserve sized to cover 95th percentile surge exposure across top-5 customers. Trigger: rolling 7-day realized token spend volatility > 20%.
2) Model-variant hedges: predefine cheaper compatible variants (quantized or smaller families) and bind routing fallback with per-customer opt-in/opt-out. Trigger: predicted margin_drop_pct > 100% for region-model.
3) Regional commit rebalancing (financial): move commit capacity between regions monthly to match forecast delta. Trigger: persistent >25% difference between forecast and actual for two consecutive weeks.
4) Marketplace swap options: contract short-term GPU-hour forward purchase (where available) in APAC markets when forecasted peak probability > 40%.

Operational knobs (automated & manual):
- Dynamic token cap (auto): reduce max_tokens by 20% on top of surge detection for latency-insensitive routes.
- Staged fallback: first try quantized variant within same region, then same model family in another region, finally a smaller family with note to user.
- Cache-first routing: prefer requests with high prefix repetition to cached nodes, raise TTL by +30% in surge.
- Price-smoothing (good for committed customers): offer time-limited token credits instead of refunds during surge times to align incentives.

Stress test examples (how to use):
- 3x daily spike for 7 days concentrated in US-West for decoder-xl -> recompute reserve_needed_usd and trigger hedges.
- Sudden 50% drop in cache hit ratio -> evaluate delta in per-token COGS and simulate whether reserve covers 30-day burn.
- Currency shock: EUR weakens by 9% against USD -> recompute regional base_cogs and margin impact for eu-west entries.

Notes on measurement and instrumentation (what to track in Console):
- Per-route 95th percentile margin (not just latency) every 10 minutes.
- Cache-hit ratio by prefix bucket and by customer cohort.
- Model fallback frequency and qualitative quality regression signal (rapid flag if >5% of requests use fallback).

Recommended next steps (short roadmap):
- Short (this sprint): wire the region/model table into the cost engine (optimize/cost-tools -> data feed) and add a surge-margin alert to Console. (Owner: Ethan Rivera)
- Mid (2–6 weeks): implement automated fallback rules for top-10 enterprise customers and run canary. (Owner: Sofia Liu)
- Long (quarter): run a Monte Carlo hedging sim (30k draws) to refine reserve sizing and publish a 90-day hedging policy. (Owner: Product-Optimize)

Open questions / risks:
- How much quality degradation can business accept when we fallback a customer? Need per-customer SLOs and an opt-out flow.
- Legal/compliance for cross-region routing for regulated customers (HIPAA/EU data residency) — we must exclude those from some hedges.
- Forward GPU contracts availability is limited in some clouds — may not be a reliable hedge for APAC.

Quick appendix (calculator snippets to paste into sheet cells):
- cell A1: =Retail_Price - Base_COGS
- cell A2: =A1 - (Base_COGS * Peak_Multiplier - Base_COGS)
- cell A3: =IF(A1=0, 0, (A1 - A2)/ABS(A1))
- reserve calc: =MAX(0, -MIN(0, A2)) * Forecast_1k_Volume

Comments for reviewers:
This is intentionally compact and pragmatic — designed to be copy/pasted into the existing regional COGS sheets as a "surge & hedging" tab. Looking for feedback on: the chosen volatility bands, whether reserve sizing should target 90th vs 95th percentile, and acceptability of the staged fallback quality tradeoffs.
